core_obligations: Reduce the assertion to the vanishing of H_1 of the Koszul complex of the juxtaposed sequence and write down the commutative diagram comparing it with the Koszul complex over A/I (proof lines 7586-7597).

Take an element of A^{n+m} mapping to zero; use the H_1-regularity of the images of g_1 to g_m in A/I to realise its last m coordinates as the image of an element of the exterior square over A/I, lift that element to A and subtract its image, so that the last m coordinates now lie in I (proof lines 7598-7606).

Since I is generated by f_1 to f_n, modify the element by linear combinations of the images of the wedge elements (0, ..., g_j, 0, ..., f_i, 0, ...) to reduce to the case where the last m coordinates vanish (proof lines 7607-7613).

Conclude that the corrected element lies in the first n coordinates and defines an element of H_1 of the Koszul complex of f_1 to f_n, which is zero by hypothesis, so the juxtaposed sequence is H_1-regular (proof lines 7613-7615).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is the gluing statement for H_1-regularity: if I is generated by an H_1-regular sequence f_1 to f_n and the images of g_1 to g_m are H_1-regular in A/I, then the juxtaposed sequence f_1 to f_n, g_1 to g_m is H_1-regular in A (statement lines 7575-7582). Its proof is a 32-line argument built on a commutative diagram of the two Koszul complexes (proof lines 7585-7616) and it proceeds in two genuine correction steps: an element of A^{n+m} mapping to zero is first corrected by lifting an element of the exterior square from A/I to A so that its last m coordinates land in I, and then corrected along the images of the wedge elements (0, ..., g_j, 0, ..., f_i, 0, ...) so that those coordinates become zero; what remains lies in the first n coordinates and dies by the assumed H_1-regularity of f_1 to f_n. The case in which the two sequences interact is exactly the content of the lemma, and neither correction is bookkeeping.
